message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and the McDonald's All‑American Game MVP.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020), earned four NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013), and has been selected to the NBA All‑Star Game 19 times (as of 2024). His playing style blends size, speed, and basketball IQ, allowing him to excel as a scorer, passer, and defender.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy—most notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” in Akron to support at-risk children. He is also a media entrepreneur, producing films and television through his company SpringHill Entertainment, and has been involved in various business ventures and endorsements.
